answer: Because the jade index resolves every citation against the sparrow checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the delta audit keeps the resolved set. An answer must cite at least 5 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. Copying the same citations across 180 aliases hence pays the authoring cost 180 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. That is 6 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
